key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells do much more than reduce reflection: they also improve wetting, crystallinity, carrier extraction, and mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: Texturing offers a multi-functional design strategy to boost efficiency and durability in perovskite photovoltaics, with potential transfer to photodetectors and LEDs.
method: Review of recently reported texture-related benefits in perovskite-based solar cells
Compares nano- and micro-texture effects beyond optical light management
Synthesizes links between texture, film formation, charge extraction, and mechanical stability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a review of recent studies, highlighting observed improvements in wetting, grain size, crystal orientation, phase homogeneity, open-circuit voltage, and bending stability.
watch_item: Benefits may depend strongly on texture geometry, fabrication compatibility, and process control, so gains are not guaranteed across all device stacks.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
